points.point: The company recorded a full impairment of a $2,701,000 vendor deposit in 2025 after the vendor filed for bankruptcy protection.
points.quote: As recovery of the deposit was deemed unlikely, the Company recorded an impairment of the full deposit during the quarter ended June 29, 2025.

points.point: The U.S. tariff environment remains subject to significant change and uncertainty resulting from ongoing litigation, administrative actions, investigations, and alternative statutory authorities.
points.quote: As a result, the U.S. tariff environment remains subject to significant change and uncertainty, including changes arising from litigation, administrative action, additional investigations and the use of alternative statutory authorities.

points.point: The timing and ultimate amount of any additional tariff refund recoveries remain subject to ongoing legal, regulatory, and administrative proceedings.
points.quote: The ultimate amount, if any, and timing of any additional recoveries remain subject to ongoing legal, regulatory, and administrative proceedings, and additional tariff refunds will be recognized when the applicable recognition criteria have been met.

points.point: During annual impairment testing, the fair value of the Banana Boat trade name exceeded its carrying value by only 2.4 percent.
points.quote: The fair value for Banana Boat trade name exceeded its carrying value by 2.4 %.

points.point: The company recorded a $37.4 million goodwill impairment loss when classifying its Feminine Care segment as held for sale prior to completing its sale.
points.quote: As of the date we determined the Feminine Care segment to be held for sale, we tested the assets within the disposal group, including goodwill, for impairment and recorded a goodwill impairment loss of $ 37.4 .

points.point: The company has not recognized an asset for potential additional refunds of IEEPA tariffs paid due to ongoing legal and regulatory uncertainties.
points.quote: As of September 30, 2026, the Company has not recognized an asset related to the potential for additional refunds of IEEPA tariffs paid.

points.point: In November 2026, Adient's Board of Directors adopted a Tax Benefits Preservation Plan to protect the value of its net operating loss carryforwards and tax assets.
points.quote: In November 2026, Adient’s Board of Directors approved and adopted a Tax Benefits Preservation Plan in an effort to help preserve the value of Adient’s U.S. net operating loss carryforwards and other tax assets.

points.point: Customer relationship intangible assets associated with certain foreign original equipment manufacturers in China were evaluated for impairment at fiscal year end due to market share losses.
points.quote: Due to persistent market share losses of certain foreign OEM’s in China, customer relationship intangible assets associated with those foreign OEM’s were assessed for impairment as of September 30, 2026.

points.point: Adient redeemed an additional $25 million aggregate principal amount of its 8.25% senior unsecured notes at a premium of $1 million in November 2026.
points.quote: In November 2026, Adient redeemed an additional $ 25 million of the 8.25 % notes with a premium of $ 1 million.

points.point: The IRS issued notices of proposed adjustments for fiscal 2021 and 2022 that could require Tyson to pay up to $127 million in additional federal taxes.
points.quote: The proposed adjustments could result in additional United States federal income tax payments of up to approximately $ 127 million, excluding interest and penalties, if the IRS ultimately prevails on all of its positions.

points.point: Tyson recorded a $217 million fixed asset impairment charge in fiscal 2026 due to its decision to close two production facilities.
points.quote: During fiscal 2026, we recorded a fixed asset impairment charge of $ 217 million as a result of our decision to close two production facilities.

points.point: The company increased its Broiler Antitrust litigation contingency accrual by $98 million during fiscal 2026 after making no additions in fiscal 2025 or 2024.
points.quote: During fiscal 2026, the Company increased the contingency accrual for claims related to these matters by $ 98 million and did not record any additional contingency accruals during fiscal 2025 or fiscal 2024.

points.point: MarineMax entered into a merger agreement on August 9, 2026, with affiliates of Safe Harbor Marinas, LLC, to become an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary.
points.quote: On August 9, 2026, we entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “Merger Agreement”) with Parent and Merger Sub, which are both affiliates of Safe Harbor Marinas, LLC, a portfolio company of Blackstone Infrastructure Partners L.P.

points.point: MarineMax recorded a non-cash pre-tax goodwill impairment of $69.1 million for its product manufacturing reporting unit in the fiscal quarter ended June 30, 2025.
points.quote: During the three months ended June 30, 2025, as a result of the declining marine industry performance and the performance of the product manufacturing reporting unit and segment due to the challenging environment, the Company recognized a non-cash, pre-tax goodwill impairment charge of $ 69.1 million related to the product manufacturing reporting unit, which was included in goodwill impairment in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.

points.point: MarineMax entered into a new credit facility providing up to $950 million in floor plan line of credit and a $150 million revolving credit facility.
points.quote: The New Credit Facility provides the Company short-term borrowing in the form of a line of credit with asset-based borrowing availability (the “Floor Plan”) of up to $ 950 million and establishes a revolving credit facility in the maximum amount of $ 150 million (including a $ 20 million swingline facility and a $ 20 million letter of credit sublimit).

points.point: Atmos Energy reached a settlement in principle for a lawsuit involving a fatal explosion in Carrollton, Texas, where plaintiffs sought over $1.0 million to $1.0 billion.
points.quote: As of the date of this filing, the parties have reached a settlement in principle.

points.point: Atmos Energy increased its aggregate litigation contingency accrual to $156.3 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $31.6 million in the prior year.
points.quote: As of September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, we had accrued $ 156.3 million and $ 31.6 million, in the aggregate for our litigation contingencies, the principal proceedings for which are described below.

points.point: Atmos Energy maintained a total-debt-to-total-capitalization ratio of 42 percent at September 30, 2026, complying with its 70 percent maximum debt covenant threshold.
points.quote: At September 30, 2026, our total-debt-to-total-capitalization ratio, as defined, was 42 percent.

points.point: Financial statements for periods prior to the spin-off were derived from Middleby and may not reflect standalone operating results and financial condition.
points.quote: As a result, the financial information included in these Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements for periods prior to completion of the Spin-off may not necessarily reflect what our financial condition, results of operations or cash flows would have been had we been a standalone company during the periods presented, including changes that occurred in our operations and capital structure as a result of becoming a separate company.

points.point: Prior to completing the spin-off, Midera recorded $1.1 million in sales to and $2.5 million in purchases from Middleby subsidiaries during the nine months ended October 3, 2026.
points.quote: Related party sales to other Middleby entities prior to completion of the Spin-off amounted to $ 1.1 million, and purchases amounted to $ 2.5 million, for the nine months ended October 3, 2026.

points.point: Middleby ceased to be a related party to the company upon completion of the spin-off on July 6, 2026.
points.quote: Upon completion of the Spin-off on July 6, 2026, Middleby ceased to be a related party to the Company.

points.point: La-Z-Boy announced the planned closure of its leased upholstery assembly plant in Mexico with operations ending at the end of the first quarter of fiscal 2027.
points.quote: During the first quarter of fiscal 2027, we announced the planned closure of our leased upholstery assembly plant in San Luis Rio Colorado ("SLRC"), Mexico with operations ceased at the end of the first quarter of fiscal 2027.

points.point: The company recorded $9.0 million of long-lived asset impairment charges and $3.4 million of severance expense during the six months ended October 24, 2026.
points.quote: As a result of this action, during the six months ended October 24, 2026, we recorded charges within the Wholesale segment of $ 9.0 million in selling, general, and administrative ("SG&A") expense for the impairment of various long-lived assets and $ 3.4 million in cost of sales primarily related to severance expense.

points.point: Accumulated goodwill impairment losses stood at $46.9 million in Corporate and Other and $20.6 million in the Wholesale segment.
points.quote: (1) Includes $ 46.9 million and $ 20.6 million of accumulated impairment losses in Corporate and Other and the Wholesale segment, respectively.

points.point: In patent litigation brought by Centripetal in France, the Paris Court indicated it will issue its decision regarding liability on January 8, 2027.
points.quote: The final hearing took place on October 8, 2026, and the Paris Court indicated that it will issue its decision as to the liability on January 8, 2027.

points.point: Cisco is unable to estimate the likelihood of loss or loss range for claims against its Brazilian subsidiary due to Brazilian judicial uncertainties.
points.quote: While we believe there is no legal basis for the alleged liability, due to the complexities and uncertainty surrounding the judicial process in Brazil and the nature of the claims asserting joint liability with the importer, we are unable to determine the likelihood of an unfavorable outcome against our Brazilian subsidiary and are unable to reasonably estimate a range of loss, if any.

points.point: Cisco's outstanding aggregate channel partner financing guarantees representing maximum potential future payments totaled $131 million as of October 24, 2026.
points.quote: The aggregate amounts of channel partner financing guarantees outstanding, representing the total maximum potential future payments under financing arrangements with third parties, was $ 131 million and $ 127 million as of October 24, 2026 and July 25, 2026, respectively.

points.point: The Walt Disney Company filed a lawsuit against the Federal Communications Commission alleging First Amendment violations regarding early broadcast license renewals for its owned television stations.
points.quote: The complaint alleges that the defendants have violated, and continue to violate, plaintiffs’ rights under the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution by launching pretextual regulatory investigations and threatening the ABC stations’ broadcast licenses through early license renewal proceedings to punish plaintiffs for content and viewpoints the administration dislikes.

points.point: Disney recorded a $1.0 billion impairment charge on its investment in A+E during fiscal year 2026.
points.quote: In fiscal 2026, the Company recorded charges of $ 1.0 billion for impairment of A+E.

points.point: DISH Network filed antitrust counterclaims challenging Disney's carriage agreements, bundling arrangements, and acquisition of a controlling interest in FuboTV.
points.quote: DISH asserts a tying claim under Sherman Act § 1 and New York’s Donnelly Act challenging certain provisions in the Company’s carriage agreement with DISH; claims under Sherman Act § 1 challenging an ESPN / Fox One bundle, the creation of Fubo Sports, and the Company’s acquisition of a controlling share of Fubo; a claim under Clayton Act § 7 challenging the Company’s acquisition of a controlling share of Fubo; and a claim under Sherman Act § 2 alleging the Company engaged in a pattern of conduct in an attempt to monopolize an alleged market for skinny sports bundles.

points.point: Two real estate developers are seeking approximately $980 million in compensatory damages in civil lawsuits regarding Hunters Point.
points.quote: The plaintiffs seek approximately $ 980 million in compensatory damages and unspecified punitive damages.

points.point: Tetra Tech recorded a $92.4 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge in the second quarter of fiscal 2025 for its Global Development Services reporting unit.
points.quote: As a result, we recorded a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $ 92.4 million included in operating income in the second quarter of fiscal 2025.

points.point: A significant portion of the company's $41.4 million in unrecognized tax benefits relates to a fiscal 2023 tax return hedging position.
points.quote: A significant portion of the uncertain tax positions is related to a hedging position taken in our fiscal 2023 tax return for which the statute is due to expire in fiscal 2027.

points.point: Spire recognized a $4.3 million after-tax impairment charge during fiscal 2026 relating to the planned divestiture of Spire Mississippi.
points.quote: The year-to-date change in net income was driven by the $48.6 improved performance of Spire Missouri and the $3.1 increase from Spire Alabama, partly offset by the $18.8 loss attributable to Spire Tennessee (Spire ownership commenced after prime earnings season) and the $4.3 (after-tax) impairment relating to the divestiture of Spire Mississippi, impacts that are excluded from adjusted earnings.

points.point: On October 6, 2026, Spire Alabama received regulatory authorization to issue up to $150.0 million in long-term debt and execute associated interest rate derivative instruments.
points.quote: On October 6, 2026, Spire Alabama Inc. received authorization from the Alabama Public Service Commission to issue and sell up to $150.0 of long-term debt and to enter into interest rate derivative instruments to lock in interest rates associated with the debt issuance.

points.point: Spire allocated goodwill to its Spire Tennessee reporting unit in fiscal 2026 following the acquisition of Piedmont Tennessee.
points.quote: In fiscal 2026, Spire recorded goodwill allocated to the Spire Tennessee reporting unit in connection with the acquisition of Piedmont Tennessee.

points.point: Sanmina recognized a $261 million contingent cash consideration liability in connection with its acquisition of ZT Systems.
points.quote: Additionally, the Company recognized a $ 261 million contingent cash consideration liability arising from the ZT Systems acquisition which is classified as other liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets.

points.point: Sanmina finalized a $6 million settlement resolving a False Claims Act qui tam lawsuit without admitting liability.
points.quote: The settlement included no admission of liability and provided for payments to the United States, Mr. Eckert, and his counsel totaling $ 6 million.

points.point: A negotiated working capital settlement with a seller led to a $243 million reduction in the total purchase consideration paid at closing for an acquisition.
points.quote: During the third quarter ended June 27, 2026, the Company finalized its post-closing working capital calculation, as a result of a negotiated settlement pursuant to the Purchase Agreement, with the seller which resulted in a $ 243 million reduction to the total purchase consideration paid at closing.

points.point: On November 10, 2026, the company entered into an agreement increasing its revolving line of credit under the U.S. Revolver from $150 million to $200 million.
points.quote: On November 10, 2026, we entered into the Commitment Increase Agreement (as defined herein) in order to, among other things, increase the amount of the revolving line of credit extended to the Company under the U.S. Revolver from $ 150 million to $ 200 million.

points.point: As of September 30, 2026, the company was contingently liable for $103.1 million in outstanding letters of credit.
points.quote: We were contingently liable for letters of credit of $ 103.1 million as of September 30, 2026.

points.point: Under its credit agreement, the company must maintain a consolidated cash balance of at least $60.0 million at all times.
points.quote: Additionally, we must maintain a consolidated cash balance of $ 60.0 million at all times, which can be deducted from the letters of credit outstanding as noted above.

points.point: As of March 31, 2026, Griffon ceased U.K. operations of the AMES Companies and recorded $27,116 in discontinued operations charges, including $19,867 of non-cash asset impairment charges.
points.quote: As of March 31, 2026, the Company ceased business operations of the AMES Companies in the U.K. and recorded charges in discontinued operations totaling $ 27,116 consisting of non-cash asset impairment charges of $ 19,867 and cash charges related to personnel-related costs and vendor agreement terminations of $ 7,249 .

points.point: Griffon received a $161,100 second-lien paid-in-kind debt receivable and a 43% equity interest upon forming the Veritage Brands joint venture on June 9, 2026.
points.quote: At closing, Griffon received $ 100,000 in cash, a $ 161,100 second-lien PIK debt receivable, and a 43 % equity interest with an initial carrying value of $ 118,600 .

points.point: Griffon responded to an EPA information request regarding the Historic Potteries site in East Trenton, New Jersey, which was added to the National Priorities List in July 2025.
points.quote: Griffon recently received, and responded to, an information request from the EPA in connection with the Historic Potteries site in East Trenton, New Jersey, which was added to the EPA’s National Priorities List in July 2025.

points.point: A putative securities class action was filed against F5 alleging false or misleading statements regarding the company's cybersecurity capabilities.
points.quote: The complaint alleges that the Company and certain of its executives made false or misleading statements in violation of Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Exchange Act of 1934 regarding the Company’s cybersecurity capabilities.

points.point: Two stockholder derivative lawsuits were filed in February 2026 alleging breach of fiduciary duty and securities law violations related to the securities class action.
points.quote: Two derivative lawsuits related to the Securities Class Action were filed in February 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington.

points.point: The court of appeals remanded a portion of Lynwood's NGINX copyright claim against F5 back to the district court for further proceedings.
points.quote: On December 2, 2024, the Court of Appeals issued its mandate returning the matter to the District Court for further proceedings on the remaining portion of the copyright claim.

points.point: Energizer recorded no accruals for its consolidated antitrust class action lawsuits because the likelihood of loss is neither probable nor estimable.
points.quote: The Company has not recorded any accruals in its consolidated financial statements as the likelihood of a loss from these cases is not probable nor estimable at this time.

points.point: In fiscal 2026, a quantitative fair value assessment of the Armor All trade name exceeded its carrying value of $228.5 million by approximately 17%.
points.quote: Based on the valuation performed as of July 1, 2026, the fair value of the trade name exceeded the carrying value of $ 228.5 by approximately 17 %.

points.point: Energizer recognized a non-cash pre-tax settlement loss of $31.8 million in fiscal 2026 following the termination and settlement of its U.K. pension plan.
points.quote: As a result, the Company realized a non-cash pre-tax settlement loss as a component of the net periodic pension cost of $ 31.8 during fiscal 2026.

points.point: Dolby recorded a $37.2 million liability following an unfavorable judgment on litigation assumed from the fiscal 2023 MPEG LA acquisition, offset by a matching indemnification asset.
points.quote: During fiscal 2026, we recognized a $ 37.2 million accrued liability related to an unfavorable judgment on litigation that we assumed as part of our acquisition of MPEG LA, L.L.C. in fiscal 2023.

points.point: Dolby recognized a $14.2 million contingent liability at acquisition date for potential payments due upon achieving specified revenue targets under an assumed agreement.
points.quote: The Company recognized a contingent liability of $ 14.2 million on the acquisition date based on a discounted cash flow valuation technique.

points.point: Dolby maintains contractual agreements with entities affiliated with its principal stockholder, the Dolby family, which jointly own commercial real estate leased for company operations.
points.quote: We maintain contractual agreements relating to certain entities affiliated with the Dolby family, who is considered a related party as our principal stockholder.

points.point: Both the Company and the Bank are subject to regulatory restrictions regarding the payment of dividends.
points.quote: The Company and the Bank are subject to regulatory restrictions on paying dividends.

points.point: None of the outstanding notional balance of interest rate contracts was associated with related-party loans as of September 30, 2026.
points.quote: As of September 30, 2026 , none of the outstanding notional balance is associated with related party loans.

points.point: The Company's Series A Preferred Stock became redeemable at its option, subject to regulatory approvals, on or after April 15, 2026.
points.quote: The Series A Preferred Stock became redeemable at the option of the Company, subject to all applicable regulatory approvals, on or after April 15, 2026.

points.point: Mueller accepted indemnification for a Superfund site claim involving a former U.S. Pipe facility, but recorded no accrual because potential costs cannot be reasonably estimated.
points.quote: Since the amounts of such costs cannot be reasonably estimated at this time, no amounts have been accrued for this matter as of September 30, 2026.

points.point: Mueller agreed to settle a cybersecurity class action lawsuit subject to an aggregate $285,000 cap, and the agreement is awaiting final court approval.
points.quote: The settlement agreement is subject to and is awaiting Court approval.

points.point: During fiscal 2026, Mueller recognized $27.8 million of strategic reorganization and other charges, including non-cash asset impairments in its Water Management Solutions segment.
points.quote: During fiscal year 2026, we incurred $ 27.8 million of strategic reorganization and other charges primarily related to certain transaction-related expenses, severance, expenses associated with our leadership transition, non-cash asset impairment expenses in our Water Management Solutions segment and costs related to the closure of our legacy brass foundry in Decatur, Illinois.

points.point: AECOM faces potential material client claims on two delayed Construction Management projects backed by $403.9 million in letters of credit and $1.0 billion in performance bonds.
points.quote: The Company has provided financial and performance assurances to the clients of these projects in the form of corporate guarantees, $ 403.9 million of standby letters of credit, and $ 1.0 billion of surety performance bonds.

points.point: Professional liability accruals classified within accrued contract costs reached $906.6 million as of September 30, 2026.
points.quote: The Company's professional liability accruals were $ 906.6 million and $ 893.7 million as of September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, and classified as accrued contract costs.

points.point: The company may incur additional costs as an indemnitor on a divested business's surety bonds, though the range of impacts cannot currently be determined.
points.quote: The Company does not have sufficient information to determine the range of potential impacts; however, it is reasonably possible that the Company may incur additional costs related to these bonds.

points.point: The company was in compliance with all financial covenants under its revolving credit agreement as of October 3, 2026.
points.quote: As of October 3, 2026, the Company was in compliance with all financial covenants under the Revolving Credit Agreement.

points.point: In September 2025, the Federal Circuit overturned a lower court decision that had invalidated a jury verdict against Google.
points.quote: In September 2025, the Federal Circuit overturned the lower court decision that had invalidated the jury verdict against Google, and is now set to decide the post-trial motions, including the Company’s motion for injunctive relief and additional damages.

points.point: During fiscal 2026, the company incurred restructuring and other charges of $7,469 thousand associated with optimizing its organizational structure, workforce, and operational footprint.
points.quote: During fiscal 2026, the Company incurred restructuring and other charges associated with optimizing its organizational structure, workforce, and operational footprint.

points.point: D.R. Horton's inventory impairment charges rose to $112.5 million in fiscal 2026 from $33.0 million in fiscal 2025, driven primarily by $91.4 million in the rental segment.
points.quote: During fiscal 2026, impairment charges totaled $ 112.5 million compared to $ 33.0 million and $ 14.0 million in fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively.

points.point: Estimated liabilities for legal contingencies increased to $1.2 billion at September 30, 2026, with approximately 99% of these reserves pertaining to construction defect matters.
points.quote: The estimated liabilities for these contingencies were $ 1.2 billion and $ 1.1 billion at September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, and are included in accrued expenses and other liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets.

points.point: Except for contractual risk transfer, the company is almost exclusively self-insured for construction defect exposures for periods after June 1, 2021.
points.quote: After June 1, 2021, except for contractual risk transfer, the Company is almost exclusively self-insured for construction defect exposures.

points.point: During fiscal 2026, the company recorded asset impairment charges of $42.6 million by writing down long-lived assets to their fair value of $41.5 million.
points.quote: During the year ended September 30, 2026, the Company wrote down long-lived assets with a carrying value of $ 84.1 million to a fair value of $ 41.5 million, resulting in recognized asset impairment charges of $ 42.6 million.

points.point: In February 2026, Greif entered into amended credit agreements to refinance its existing borrowings and support ongoing working capital, capital expenditures, and acquisitions.
points.quote: On February 27, 2026, the Company and certain of its subsidiaries entered into a third amended and restated senior secured credit agreement with a syndicate of financial institutions and an amended and restated senior secured credit agreement with CoBank, ACB and other farm credit lending institutions (collectively, the “2026 Credit Agreements”).

points.point: During 2026, Greif closed or divested five plants and severed 467 employees as part of its restructuring efforts.
points.quote: There were five plants closed or divested in 2026 and a total of 467 employees severed throughout 2026 as part of the Company’s restructuring efforts.
